For everyday users

Process Mining Work-Bench
Quick-Start Guide

A short, step-by-step walk through a simple analysis — from signing in to sharing what you find — using only the features available to a standard user.

This guide follows one path end to end: sign in → open a project → read the A-Chart → filter → compare with A/B → record your findings. Everything here is available without any special role — no setup or administration required.
1

Sign in

Open the Work-Bench in your browser and enter your username and password. If your organisation requires it, you will then confirm a 6-digit code from your authenticator app, or sign in with a passkey (Touch ID, Windows Hello or a security key).

TipThe background image and the version line are set by your administrator — they do not affect how you sign in.
2

Find your data

After signing in you land in the Work-Bench: the sidebar on the left, an empty chart area on the right. Open the Connections section and click the connection your administrator assigned to you. A green dot shows you are connected.

TipCreating or editing connections is an administrator task, so you will not see a ＋ button here — just pick the one that was shared with you.
3

Open a project

Open the Projects section and select a project. The A-Chart loads automatically and the sidebar tidies its sections away so the map has room.

TipA project is one process — for example an order-to-cash flow or a support workflow.
4

Read the A-Chart

The A-Chart is your process map, discovered directly from the data. Boxes are steps, arrows are the transitions between them, and a thicker arrow means the selected metric is higher. The tiles across the top (KPIs) summarise the filtered data.

TipMap vocabulary: a node is a step, an arrow is a transition, a dashed box is a group of steps, and the tiles above are KPIs.
5

Choose a metric

The Metrics chips decide what the arrow thickness means: Count, Percentage (share of a step’s outgoing journeys), Journey % (share of all journeys), or the transition times Avg, Min, Max and Std Dev. Exactly one is active at a time.

TipEach chart view remembers its own metric independently.
6

Filter to your question

The Filters section narrows the picture: a date range, steps that must or must not appear, how many steps a journey has, how long it took, its score, and up to three business (meta) fields. An active filter shows a badge; the ⊗ clears just that one. Save a useful combination as a preset to reuse later.

TipFilters drive everything at once — the map, the KPIs and every other view update together.
7

Follow a single case

Switch the view menu to Individual Journey, type an Event ID in the sidebar and press Load Journey. One case is drawn step by step, with the time shown on each node and its own KPI tiles above.

8

Bring in a second view (B-Chart)

The B-Chart is a second, fully independent process map with its own filters and its own layout. Use it to set up a “before vs after” or “region A vs region B” picture.

9

Compare side by side (A/B Comparison)

A/B Comparison puts panel A and panel B next to each other, with a similarity badge along the bottom, so you can see at a glance how the two filtered pictures differ.

TipSet the filters on each panel first (in A-Chart and B-Chart), then switch to A/B Comparison to view them together.
10

Dig into the numbers (Statistics)

The Statistics view lists the most common routes (journey variants) in a sortable table, above a journeys-over-time chart. Sort to find the busiest or the rarest paths.

11

Capture what you find (Notes)

Add a note to any step or transition to record an observation. Give it a title and an importance; it keeps the exact filter context so it still makes sense later. You and your colleagues can search, filter and mark notes as resolved.

12

Optional: AI-supported Documentation

If your connection has an AI model attached, the AI supported Documentation view turns the current A-Chart and its context into a written report you can save as a PDF. The cards shown before you run it summarise exactly what will be sent.

TipYou can generate the report; editing the underlying analysis prompt is reserved for advanced users.
13

Help, preferences & your account

The ? button (or ⌘/Ctrl + /) opens the floating Help panel. The Configuration section holds display preferences — theme, font sizes and KPI order. At the very bottom of the sidebar you can manage two-factor / passkeys and sign out.

Beyond the basics

A few features are hidden from everyday users because they change shared data or configuration. They need a Power user, Developer or Administrator role:

  • Journey Sampling
  • Conformance Check and Happy Path
  • Simulation
  • Creating or editing connections
  • Editing the AI analysis prompt
  • The Action Designer and Integration console
  • The Administration site

If you need one of these, ask your administrator — nothing you do as a standard user can change another person’s data or the system’s configuration.
